solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Monotonous speaker curtailed by “Cor blimey, naked bird” (6,6)

indicators.note: to curtail is to cut off the tail, so the last letter goes
stripped of its covering, so the word loses its outside letters

blocks.note: a DRONE talks monotonously; curtailed, it loses its E
CRIKEY = blimey; stripped of C and Y

annotation.surface: A Cockney listener exclaims at a boring talker interrupted by a bare bird.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cor blimey" looks like one exclamation but splits into two: Cor for GOSH and blimey for CRIKEY. A drongo-shrike is an African bird.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain name-for-kind definition: the drongo-shrike (drongo) is an African songbird.

entries.clue: Clamour to support nude dancing in New Zealand city (7)

indicators.note: letters that dance move around into a new order
in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath

annotation.surface: A noisy crowd cheers on naked dancers somewhere in New Zealand.
annotation.walkthrough: Clamour comes first in the clue but last in the answer, because in a down entry supporting means going below.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Dunedin is one of New Zealand's South Island cities.

entries.clue: Like precious stone from old friend in Eton, originally (7)

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone describes a gem-like quality once found in an old school friend at Eton.
annotation.walkthrough: "from" separates definition and wordplay. Eton is the famous English boarding school, but only its first letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Opaline is the adjective from opal, a gemstone, so it means resembling one.

entries.clue: Method to transfer power damaged great source of water (4,5)

indicators.note: a damaged word is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: rain is where water comes from

annotation.surface: A broken dam or pump has hurt a great water supply.
annotation.walkthrough: Only the first word is scrambled; the source of water is added unchanged, and the letters then split at a different point to make the two-word answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A gear train, meshed gears passing motion shaft to shaft, is one engineering method of transmitting power.

entries.clue: Criticise some Tesla technicians (5)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are taken

annotation.surface: Someone complains about the engineers at Tesla.
annotation.walkthrough: To slate is British for to criticise harshly, as a reviewer slates a play.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in British usage, where reviewers slate a bad play.

entries.clue: Wine box is upside-down, but not cold (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word upside down reverses it
tells you to leave a letter out

blocks.note: a canister is a box or tin
C = cold, as on a tap; removed from the end

annotation.surface: A wine crate has been stood on its head but is no longer chilled.
annotation.walkthrough: CANISTER turned over gives RETSINAC, and dropping the C leaves the Greek resin-flavoured wine.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a resin-flavoured Greek white is one kind of wine.

entries.clue: Dresses Kelvin behind a northern station’s entrance (7)

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: K is the symbol for kelvin

annotation.surface: Someone called Kelvin is standing behind the entrance to a station up north.
annotation.walkthrough: "behind" looks like a placing instruction for Kelvin, but it is a piece in its own right: AFT.
annotation.definitionFit: Kaftans, long loose robes, are a kind of dress, so plural matches plural.

entries.clue: Way to conceive of painting More novel (12)

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

annotation.surface: An art critic suggests how to imagine a portrait of Thomas More in a new way.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital on More points to Sir Thomas More, and "novel" to a book, but both are just letters and an anagram signal. "Conceive" means become pregnant, not imagine.
annotation.definitionFit: Conceive in the pregnancy sense: impregnation is the process by which it happens.

entries.clue: State of motion, ultimately, in a tiny particle spinning (7)

indicators.note: the ultimate letter is the last one
one piece goes inside another
a spinning word turns round, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: last letter of motion, placed inside: ANAT(N)OM

annotation.surface: A physicist describes a spinning atom's state of motion.
annotation.walkthrough: "State of motion" reads as one physics phrase, but the definition is just State, the US one.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the Treasure State is one of the fifty US states.

entries.clue: Acting to prevent illness, colonist provided essential pieces of alum (7)

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, its middle letters

annotation.surface: A settler used alum as a medicine to ward off disease.
annotation.walkthrough: "Colonist" suggests a human settler, but it is the insect that lives in colonies.
annotation.definitionFit: A prefix compound: anti- plus flu, describing a remedy that acts against influenza.

entries.clue: They restore plush fitting? (12)

indicators.note: the letters are fitted together into a new order

annotation.surface: A description of tradespeople who repair luxurious fabric furnishings.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: upholsterers do restore plush, the fabric fitted to chairs.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes the trade exactly: these craftsmen renew plush upholstery on chairs.

entries.clue: Source of anger studied then overlooked, reportedly (3,4)

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the words are judged by sound

annotation.surface: Someone who read something and then missed it gets cross.
annotation.walkthrough: READ in the past tense rhymes with bed, which is what makes RED work.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the red mist is the sudden fury that descends, the source of anger boiling over.

entries.clue: Drunk happiest when son scratched inscription (7)

indicators.note: a drunk word staggers into a new order
a scratched runner is withdrawn, so the letter is removed

annotation.surface: A drunkard is at their happiest when their son scrawls a message.
annotation.walkthrough: Take the S out of HAPPIEST and rearrange the seven letters left. "when" just links the instructions.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the words carved on a gravestone are that kind of inscription.

entries.clue: Singer Vincent claiming head of investment lamped servant? (5)

indicators.note: to claim is to take in, so one piece holds another
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Gene Vincent, 1950s rock and roll singer
first letter of investment, placed inside the singer

annotation.surface: A rock singer hits a servant with a lamp after taking over the head of investment.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lamped" in slang means punched, but here it means kept in a lamp, like Aladdin's genie; the question mark flags the play.
annotation.definitionFit: The question mark admits a playful coinage: the genie in Aladdin's lamp serves whoever rubs it.

entries.clue: Cut Jack up in disgust in assessment (9)

indicators.note: a cut word is shortened by its last letter
one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: RAISE = jack up; cut, it loses its E; placed inside the word for disgust

annotation.surface: In an evaluation, someone disgusted cuts a man called Jack down to size.
annotation.walkthrough: Jack looks like a name, but "Jack up" is the verb for lifting, as with a car jack.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an evaluation of worth.

entries.clue: Official stopping trouble before departure (9)

indicators.note: a stopper sits in a hole, so one piece plugs the inside of another

blocks.note: a plight is a troubled situation
a referee is an official; placed inside the word for trouble

annotation.surface: A referee is blocking a difficulty before someone leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: PREFLIGHT is an adjective, and "before departure" works adjectivally too, as in preflight checks.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective for adjective: preflight checks happen before an aircraft departs.

entries.clue: Immediately name boring American “Pierce” (2,1,6)

indicators.note: something boring drills into another, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a tag is a name label; it bores into A...LANCE

annotation.surface: Someone instantly calls an American called Pierce dull.
annotation.walkthrough: "Boring" looks like a description of Pierce, but it tells the name to drill into the other pieces. Pierce, capitalised as a first name, is really the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: understood at a glance means understood in an instant.

entries.clue: Endure starting late journey with legs apart (7)

indicators.note: a word that starts late misses its first letter

annotation.surface: A rider who set off late puts up with a long, bow-legged trip.
annotation.walkthrough: Endure has to be read as the verb last, as in make it last.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sitting astride a horse means sitting with a leg on each side.

entries.clue: Satirise a politician interrupting simpleton (7)

indicators.note: an interruption breaks into something, so it goes inside

blocks.note: A + MP (Member of Parliament); placed inside the word for simpleton

annotation.surface: A politician keeps cutting in on a fool and mocking him.
annotation.walkthrough: MP means Member of Parliament, the standard politician in British clues.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to mock through satire.

entries.clue: Glimpse location for audition (5)

indicators.note: audition is hearing, so the word is judged by its sound

annotation.surface: A casting venue for actors being glimpsed.
annotation.walkthrough: "Audition" suggests a casting, but here it means hearing, so SITE is heard as SIGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb for verb: sailors sight land when they first glimpse it.

entries.clue: Yellow, after spilling guts in emergency? It’s possibly a nasty infection (7)

indicators.note: a word whose guts spill out keeps only its outer letters
one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: an emergency tyre is a spare
outer letters of YelloW, placed inside the word for emergency

annotation.surface: A coward is gutted in a crisis, and the result may be a horrible infection.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds medical, but the infection is on a computer; "possibly" signals spyware is only one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by possibly: malicious software infects a computer much as a germ infects a body.

entries.clue: Stop working, as setter’s restricted by painful condition (4,3)

indicators.note: restricted means held in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints
the setter has = I have = I'VE; placed inside the painful condition

annotation.surface: The crossword setter admits to being laid up with a painful illness.
annotation.walkthrough: "Setter's" is short for setter has, and the setter refers to themself as I, so it gives I'VE.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: an engine or knee that gives out has stopped working.

entries.clue: Strip of land is so close for naturism breaks (7)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter
the letter breaks into the word, going inside

blocks.note: last letter of naturism, breaking into TH(M)US

annotation.surface: A narrow beach is kept nearly off-limits because nudists keep interrupting.
annotation.walkthrough: IS stays as printed; the M goes into THUS, not into IS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain geographical term for a narrow neck of land joining two larger areas, as at Panama.

entries.clue: Diet energy gunk (5)

annotation.surface: A slimming product turns out to be energy goo.
annotation.walkthrough: Diet has to be read as a verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are sticky, unpleasant goo.

entries.clue: Rest of America always entertained by partner (7)

indicators.note: a host entertains a guest inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: ay (or aye) = always, an old word; placed inside the word for partner

annotation.surface: An American is forever being wined and dined by a partner.
annotation.walkthrough: "of America" belongs to the definition: layover is the American word for a stopover, which Britons call a break in the journey.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: layover is the American word for a stopover rest on a journey.

entries.clue: Blessed, perhaps in retirement, one receives zero capital (7)

indicators.note: Blessed is one example of a bearer of the name, not a synonym
a retiring piece draws back, so it reads backwards
to receive is to take in, so a piece goes inside

blocks.note: Brian Blessed, the booming British actor; BRIAN reversed
O looks like zero; received inside the other letters

annotation.surface: A retired holy man takes in nothing at all.
annotation.walkthrough: "Blessed" is not holy but a surname: Brian Blessed is a loud-voiced British actor, so Blessed perhaps = BRIAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: Kenya's seat of government is a capital city.

entries.clue: Allure of love affair started by girl on vacation (7)

indicators.note: a vacated word is emptied, keeping only its outer letters
one piece comes at the start of the other

blocks.note: an amour is a love affair

annotation.surface: A holiday romance begun by a young woman has a certain allure.
annotation.walkthrough: "On vacation" sounds like a holiday, but it means vacated: the word is emptied.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: attractive, alluring charm.

entries.clue: Check clothing for second venture? (12)

blocks.note: to rein in is to check

annotation.surface: Someone asks to have their clothes inspected before a second attempt.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as playful: reinvestment is investing again, a second venture of money.
annotation.definitionFit: The question mark flags a playful reading: putting money in again is a second venture.
